guarantees.claim: state_q is the registered version of state_d, resetting synchronously to StCtrlDataIdle.
guarantees.cond: Every clock edge (and async/sync reset if implemented inside the macro).

guarantees.claim: The PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM macro enforces that state_q never holds an illegal 10-bit encoding outside the six defined state_e members; on detection of an invalid encoding it forces state_q to StCtrlDataIdle.
guarantees.cond: If state_d or state_q ever becomes a value not in {StCtrlDataIdle, StCtrlDataHwEn, StCtrlDataSwEn, StCtrlDataDis, StCtrlDataWait, StCtrlDataInvalid}.

assumptions.claim: During normal operation, the combinational logic driving state_d produces only one of the six valid state_e encodings.
assumptions.cond: Always when the key manager is not in error recovery.
assumptions.risk: If an invalid value is driven onto state_d, the PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM will detect it and force state_q to StCtrlDataIdle, potentially disrupting the data‑enable state machine and causing loss of key‑management control.

uncertain_points.claim: The exact error‑reporting mechanism (alert, fatal flag, etc.) inside PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM is not visible from this chunk; an illegal state encoding may be silently forced to Idle without notifying the system.
uncertain_points.cond: Whenever state_d or state_q becomes corrupted.
uncertain_points.risk: A temporary or permanent FSM corruption could go undetected, leading to unauthorized key‑manager operations or deadlock.

uncertain_points.claim: If the macro resets state_q to StCtrlDataIdle after detecting an invalid encoding, there is no visible sideband signal (e.g., error status, interrupt) propagated outside this module to inform higher‑level key manager logic.
uncertain_points.cond: After a fault injection or SEU flips state bits.
uncertain_points.risk: The data‑enable state machine may silently restart from Idle, possibly leaving data paths in an inconsistent security state or causing glitches in key access control.
